database_note: The movies table holds core film details, while ratings, director_mapping, genre, and role_mapping record specific events or transactions linking people to films. The names table serves as a lookup for person descriptions. Connect these by joining movies.id to ratings.movie_id, director_mapping.movie_id, genre.movie_id, and role_mapping.movie_id. Link people via names.id to director_mapping.name_id and role_mapping.name_id. The ERD table is metadata only; ignore it for data analysis. Do not use the comma-separated known_for_movies column for joins, as it is not a proper foreign key. This structure allows you to combine movie metadata with ratings, genres, directors, and cast members using the movie and name identifiers.
database_fact: The movies table holds core film details. The ratings, director_mapping, genre, and role_mapping tables record specific events or transactions linking people to films. The names table serves as a lookup for person descriptions. The ERD table is metadata only. The movies table connects to the ratings, director_mapping, genre, and role_mapping tables via movies.id to ratings.movie_id, director_mapping.movie_id, genre.movie_id, and role_mapping.movie_id. The names table connects to the director_mapping and role_mapping tables via names.id to director_mapping.name_id and role_mapping.name_id. The movies table contains a comma-separated known_for_movies column.
